entries.title: Psalms 115:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Are like them - As void of all sense or reason as their images.

entries.title: Psalms 115:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Ye that fear - All of you who worship the true God, not only Israelites, but even Gentile proselytes.

entries.title: Psalms 115:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Mindful - In our former straits, and therefore we trust he will still bless us.

entries.title: Psalms 115:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Both small - Of whatsoever quality, high and low, rich and poor.

entries.title: Psalms 115:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The Lord's - In a peculiar manner, where he dwelleth in that light and glory, to which no man can approach. Given - As the foregoing verse declares, that God was the creator of heaven and earth, so this asserts that he is also their Lord and governor to dispose of all men and things as he pleases.

entries.title: Psalms 115:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Silence - Into the place of silence, the grave. CHAPT. 116. This psalm is a solemn thanksgiving to God. Wherein the psalmist professes his love to God, for delivering him out of great straits and dangers, ver. 1 - 8. Prays for his future protection, and promises to praise him, and to walk holy before him, 9 - 19.
